evidence: All five task prompts explicitly say 'Evaluate the live Colderwater playground at http://localhost:3000 with Playwright MCP' (gates/render/prompt.md:3; gates/constraints/prompt.md:3; scored/functional,polish,visual/prompt.md:5). Render judge.toml:23 requires real authored editing, Run and two button clicks; Constraints judge.toml:32 requires actual Save and independent clean-context retrieval; scored prompts:3 require live authored execution before scoring. These genuinely rule out whole-dimension first-paint/static-shell success. However gates/constraints/prompt.md:7 explicitly says 'Reading loaded assets is permitted only to determine whether a prohibited ready-made editor implements the actual document surface'; gates/constraints/judge.toml:23 directs 'Use rendered DOM and browser-loaded asset evidence when needed' for a hard prerequisite. The generic ban at prompt.md:3 is only 'read implementation files to infer functional success', so it does not prohibit this technology/provenance source-based verdict. Workbook Quality Checks!D26 and Internal Quality Checks!D26 exclude scoring from source; frozen staged-task-contract.md, prompt.md section, says no prompt may derive a verdict from submission source. Public ui.md:3 does require a custom editor, so this is a conflict between a genuine architecture ask and the browser-only judge policy, not an invented public requirement. Four other dimension prompts have no corresponding implementation-source scoring exception. All frozen task/rules bytes match manifest hashes; the 10 current evidence-index artifacts also match their recorded SHA256. Those artifacts are not configured judge evidence for this conflict.
counterexample: A judge opens the live app and sees a DOM-rendered editor, then reads its loaded JavaScript bundle to determine that an imported ready-made editor implements the surface and fails cw_custom_document_surface solely on that implementation evidence. Constraints prompt.md:7 and judge.toml:23 explicitly authorize that source-derived hard-gate decision; live browser navigation does not cure it. A handwritten custom DOM editor with a heavily minified bundle is a conforming alternative: rendered editing behavior alone cannot establish its provenance, and the prompt supplies no browser-only rule for that ambiguity. These are source-review counterexamples, not measured classifier or judge failures; unrelated parser/formatter package-name matches are already excluded by the prompt and are not alleged defects.
suggested_fix: Remove the implementation-asset scoring exception, grade the live surface and editing behavior through browser observations, and resolve the mandatory editor-provenance requirement explicitly with the owner through separately authorized verification rather than silently turning a browser judge into a source reviewer.
